Topic1.Title: Open Comment on South Boulder Rec Center and Pool
Topic1.Summary: Many residents, youth, and athletes spoke in favor of preserving the South Boulder Recreation Center and its pool, citing walkability, health, and community value. Speakers criticized the data and options staff presented and urged the city to fund a rebuild or retain core amenities. Several speakers said the center serves as a safe after-school and senior gathering place.

Topic2.Title: Open Comment on Tipped Wage Credit
Topic2.Summary: Several speakers, including tipped workers, a labor organizer, and a health clinic specialist, urged council to oppose any increase to the tip credit, arguing it would cut take-home pay and worsen affordability. Restaurant owners and the Barha representative were not heard in this segment, though one speaker noted small business struggles. Speakers emphasized inflation, wage theft, and inconsistent tips.

Topic3.Title: Open Comment on Other Issues (Airport, Bears, Open Space, Israel and Flock)
Topic3.Summary: Speakers addressed unleaded aviation fuel at the airport, bear conflict and electric fencing ordinance updates, and the proposed open space tax ballot measure. One speaker criticized Flock Safety surveillance contracts and called for divestment. Staff responded that the fencing ordinance proposal is under consideration for future council action.

Topic4.Title: Arts Week Declaration
Topic4.Summary: Council presented a proclamation declaring April 3 to 12, 2026 as Boulder Arts Week and recognized Dr. Nicholas Felder as the Bright Futures Award recipient. Felder accepted on behalf of the arts community and spoke to the Boulder Arts Blueprint. Staff noted Boulder's creative sector strength and economic impact.

Topic5.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic5.Summary: Council approved consent agenda items 4A through 4Q, including a 10-year water lease with the Town of Erie and a water supply framework resolution for area 3. Council member Adams voted no on the area 3 service expansion item. Council discussed the Erie lease, which staff said would not jeopardize local water supply during drought watch.

Topic6.Title: Call-Up Items and Site Review at College Avenue
Topic6.Summary: Council reviewed call-up items including a Boulder Jewish Commons synagogue amendment, a water tap request in area 3, and a student housing site review at 1128 29th Street and 2895 East College Avenue. A motion to refer the College Avenue project to the Design Advisory Board was withdrawn after staff said the board had already reviewed and approved the design. Landmark alteration for an accessory building in Mapleton Hill was also listed.

Topic7.Title: Short-Term Festival Lodging Rental Ordinance (Second Reading)
Topic7.Summary: Council held a public hearing and adopted Ordinance 8743, expanding festival lodging rental licenses to tenants with owner consent and to vacant units in properties with long-term rental licenses. Staff said applications open the next day and licenses issue May 4 for Sundance. Council discussed revenue splits, renter protections, and a possible vacant-only option that was not adopted, and the vote was 8 to 0.

Topic8.Title: Tip Offset Options and Timeline
Topic8.Summary: Staff presented the tip credit authority options after council's retreat priority and reviewed economic, labor, and equity considerations, including restaurant sales tax and employment trends. Options included status quo, moderate increases, a higher offset, and maximized offset, with council narrowing to status quo, Option 2A, Option 2B, and a Benjamin proposal to pause the tipped wage through 2029. Council directed staff to return with more data and considered a later public hearing aligned with student availability, with CAC to help schedule.
